1.overview: Nebuchadnezzar takes Jerusalem and brings some of the temple vessels and young men of Judah, including Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah, to Babylon for training in the king’s service. Daniel secures a ten-day diet of vegetables and water for the four, and God grants them health, learning, and wisdom, while Daniel gains insight into visions and dreams.

sections.heading: Jerusalem’s Defeat and the Young Men’s Training
The Young Men Enter the King’s Service

2.overview: Nebuchadnezzar demands that Babylon’s wise men reveal and interpret his troubling dream, and orders their execution when they cannot. After God reveals the mystery to Daniel, Daniel recounts the statue and interprets it as successive kingdoms overcome by God’s everlasting kingdom, and Nebuchadnezzar promotes Daniel and his friends.

sections.heading: Daniel seeks and receives the mystery
Daniel recounts and interprets the dream
Daniel and his friends are promoted

3.overview: Nebuchadnezzar erects a golden statue on the plain of Dura and commands officials and people of every nation to worship it or face the furnace; after astrologers accuse Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, the king threatens them, and they refuse to worship his gods. Nebuchadnezzar orders them into the furnace, but they emerge unharmed with a fourth figure seen in the fire, prompting the king to praise their God, issue a decree protecting his worship, and promote the three men in Babylon.

sections.heading: The Golden Statue and Worship Decree
The Furnace and the Men’s Deliverance

4.overview: Nebuchadnezzar recounts his dream of a great tree cut down at a heavenly decree, and Daniel interprets it as the king’s coming humbling until he recognizes that the Most High rules human kingdoms. After the decree is fulfilled and Nebuchadnezzar loses his reason, he looks to heaven, is restored to sanity and kingship, and praises the King of heaven.

sections.heading: The Dream of the Great Tree

5.overview: Belshazzar’s feast profanes the Jerusalem temple vessels, and a hand writes on the palace wall; when Babylon’s wise men cannot interpret the inscription, the queen recommends Daniel. Daniel recounts Nebuchadnezzar’s humbling, condemns Belshazzar’s pride, interprets the writing as the end of his reign and kingdom, and sees Belshazzar slain as Darius the Mede receives the kingdom.

6.overview: Darius appoints Daniel over the kingdom, and jealous officials exploit a decree against prayer to have Daniel thrown into a lions’ den. God delivers Daniel, the accusers are condemned, and Darius proclaims the power and enduring kingdom of Daniel’s God.

sections.heading: Daniel’s rise and the officials’ plot
The decree and Daniel in the den
Daniel’s deliverance and the accusers’ fate

7.overview: Daniel records a vision of four beasts rising from the sea, followed by the Ancient of Days holding court and giving everlasting dominion to one like a Son of Man. An angel explains that the beasts are kings and kingdoms, while the fourth kingdom and its arrogant horn oppress the saints until judgment removes the horn’s power and the saints receive the kingdom.

sections.heading: Daniel’s Vision of the Four Beasts
The Court and the Son of Man

8.overview: In a vision at Susa, Daniel sees a two-horned ram overcome by a goat, whose great horn breaks and is replaced by four horns; a little horn then attacks the host, the daily sacrifice, and the sanctuary. Gabriel interprets the beasts as the kings of Media and Persia and the king of Greece, explains the little horn’s rise and destruction, and says the sanctuary will be restored after 2,300 evenings and mornings; Daniel remains shaken and unable to understand the vision.

sections.heading: The Ram, the Goat, and the Little Horn

9.overview: In Darius’s first year, Daniel understands from Jeremiah’s prophecy that Jerusalem’s desolation will last seventy years and prays, confessing Israel’s sin and asking God to restore Jerusalem and its sanctuary. Gabriel comes to Daniel and explains the seventy weeks decreed for his people and holy city, including Jerusalem’s rebuilding, the Messiah’s being cut off, the city and sanctuary’s destruction, and the final desolation.

10.overview: Daniel receives a vision of a radiant man beside the Tigris after three weeks of mourning and fasting, and the vision leaves him weak and speechless. A messenger explains that the prince of Persia delayed his response until Michael helped, strengthens Daniel, and describes conflict with the princes of Persia and Greece before revealing what will happen to Daniel’s people.

11.overview: The vision traces Persian and Greek rulers, then recounts wars between the kings of the North and South, including failed alliances, invasions, and shifts of power. It describes a contemptible ruler who attacks the holy covenant, desecrates the temple, and persecutes the faithful, before concluding with a final campaign and his death without help.

sections.heading: Wars between the North and South
The contemptible king and the covenant

12.overview: Michael rises during a time of unprecedented distress, when Daniel’s people whose names are in the book are delivered; the dead awake to everlasting life or contempt, and the wise shine. Daniel seals the words, then hears that the wonders last for a time, times, and half a time, receives the periods of 1,290 and 1,335 days, and is told he will rest and later rise to his inheritance.

sections.heading: The Sealed Words and Daniel’s Inheritance
